investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing via Shared ELB Dependency
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-29T12:30–12:31Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at the /v1/agents endpoint during agent provisioning. Because the failure is shared across every sibling check with the same error message and zero evidence was collected, the root cause is localized to the swarm gateway layer (the AWS ELB fronting /v1/agents), not to the eval runner or any individual check's logic.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 serving POST /v1/agents — was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agent check calls POST /api/agents, which proxies to that ELB; all three returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". Because the failure occurred at the very first network hop (agent creation), no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever produced, satisfying zero of the four required contract fields. This is an eval-detected infrastructure availability issue localized to the swarm gateway ELB; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — the most strongly supported cause given the identical 502 across all three checks.
Transient network partition or security-group/firewall rule change between the production-api and the ELB, causing all outbound connections to /v1/agents to be refused.
The ELB target group drained all healthy instances (e.g., a deployment, scaling event, or crash loop) causing the load balancer to return 502 with no available backends.
DNS resolution failure or ELB endpoint rotation that left the production-api pointing at a stale or unreachable ELB address.
A misconfigured swarm gateway service (e.g., wrong port, missing TLS termination, or changed path prefix) that causes the ELB to reject all inbound requests with 502.
